description: Maintain an n by n by n binary matrix and support setting or clearing a cell. Query the layer index containing the most ones; ties go to the largest layer index. Example 1: in a three-layer matrix, setting two cells in layer 0 and one in layer 2 makes largestMatrix return 0. Example 2: when all layers contain zero ones, the tie rule returns n - 1. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 100, coordinates are in range, and there are at most 100000 updates and 10000 queries.
intuition: Only the count for the changed layer can move, and a priority queue can expose the highest count with the required index tie-break.

brute_force.approach: Store all cells, then scan every layer and count its ones for every query.

optimal.approach: Store each layer as bytes, maintain its one-count, and lazily validate a heap ordered by count descending and layer descending.
optimal.time: setCell/unsetCell O(log q), largestMatrix O(1) amortized

edge_cases: Setting an already-set cell or clearing an already-clear cell must not change a count.
The largest layer index wins ties, including the all-zero initial state.
